questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of refraction of light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red colour of setting sun.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon of** refraction of light** is the shift in the path of light as it travels from one medium to another.
 
• Red colour of setting sun__:
 __
 
• It is ​due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.
 
• The Sun is very low in the sky at sunrise and sunset.
 
• Because of its short wavelength, blue light is dispersed more forcefully by the atmosphere, and it tends to be scattered numerous times and redirected away in various directions before reaching us.
 
• We perceive the longer wavelength yellow and red light as the sunshine travels a larger distance.
 
• As a result, the sky appears to be red in colour.
 
 
 
• A pencil submerged in a glass of water **appears bent **at the **water-air interface**, for example.
 
• The ray of light **bends towards normal **as it moves from a **rarer to a denser medium**, and **away from normal** as it moves from a **denser to a rarer** medium.
 
• **Lenses, magnifying glasses, prisms, and rainbows **are all possible because of this bending through refraction.
 
• **Laws of Refraction: **
 
 
• The incident ray, the refracted ray, and the normal at the point of incidence, all lie in the same plane.
 
• The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence and sine of the angle of refraction is constant.
 
 
 
• The ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the second medium of greater density is used to determine the Refractive Index. 
 
 
• The higher the refractive index, the slower light travels, causing a proportionately greater change in light direction within the material.
 
 
 
• The **velocity of light c** of a particular wavelength in empty space divided by its** velocity v** in a substance, or **n = c/v**, is also known as the** refractive index.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Image formation by the human eye__:**

 __
 
• The** majority of refraction** in the eye occurs when light rays pass through the **eye's curved, front surface** (cornea).
 
• Light rays **converge** most at the cornea and when entering and exiting the lens, forming a** picture **on the retina.
 
• Rays from the object's top and bottom are traced, resulting in an** inverted actual image** on the retina.
 
 
 
• **Formation of the rainbow__:**
 __
 
• Rainbows are created when sunlight is scattered by water droplets (such as raindrops or fog) in a process known as **refraction.**
 
• When sunlight passes through a **medium denser than air**, such as a** raindrop**, it refracts, changing its direction.
 
• When light enters the raindrop, it is** refracted, reflected off the back**, and then** refracted again** as it escapes and travels to our eyes.
 
 
 
• **Twinkling of stars__:**​
 
 
• The twinkling of a star is caused by starlight being **refracted** by the atmosphere.
 
• When starlight enters the earth's atmosphere, it undergoes** constant refraction** before reaching the surface.
 
• Atmospheric refraction takes place in a material with a** fluctuating refractive index.**
 
• The apparent location of the star differs significantly from its real position due to the **atmosphere's bending** of starlight **towards the normal.**
 
• When viewed near the horizon, the star appears slightly **higher **(above) than its real position.
 
• Because the stars are so far away, they resemble **point sources of light.**
 
• The** apparent position **of the star changes throughout time, as does the amount of starlight that enters the eye.
 
• The star flickers, seeming brighter and fainter at different periods, causing the** twinkling effect.**

__
 
• Chandragupta II, commonly known as **Vikramaditya**, was a great ruler of **northern India** who reigned from** 380 AD to 415 AD**.
 
• He was the **grandson **of **Chandragupta I** and the son of **Samudra Gupta. **
 
• Chandragupta-II's mother was **queen Datta or Dattadevi**, described as **Mahadevi.**
 
 
• The **conquest of Sakas** was the most significant event during Chandragupta II's reign.
 
 
 
• He issued silver coins in the memory of his victory over Sakas. He was the **first Gupta ruler to issue silver coins **and adopted the titles **Sakari** and **Vikramaditya**.
 
• His victory over **Malwa** aided the Malwa region's growth, and **Ujjain **became a **commercial center.**
 
• **Mehrauli Iron Pillar Inscription **(near Kutub Minar, Delhi) says that the king defeated the confederacy of **Vangas **and **Vahilkas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

He strengthened his kingdom by the matrimonial alliance with the powerful family of Lichchhavis who were the rulers of Mithila. His marriage to Lichchhvi princess **Kumaradevi**, brought him enormous power, resources, and prestige. He started the **Gupta era** in 319-320 AD.
 
• **Ramagupta **- According to 'Devi Chandragupta' (Vishakhadatta), Samudragupta was succeeded by Ramagupta. It seems that Ramagupta ruled for a very short period. He was the **only Gupta ruler to issue 'copper' coins**. 
 
• **Kumaragupta II **- He was an emperor of the Gupta Empire. An image of Gautama Buddha at Sarnath notes that he succeeded Purugupta who was most likely his father. He was succeeded by Budhagupta. Several statues of the standing Buddha, representative of Gupta art, are known from the reign of Kumaragupta II, now in the Sarnath Museum.

questions.question: The area of a circular park is 1386 m². If a path of the width 7 m is laid around and inside the park. Then the area of the path is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The area of a circular park = 1386 m²

A path of the width = 7 m

**Formula used:**

Area of circle = πr²

**Calculation:**

According to the question

Area of circle = πr²

⇒ 22/7 × r² = 1386 m²

⇒ 22r²/7 = 1386

⇒ r²/7 = 63

⇒ r² = 441 

⇒ r = 21 m

Now,

Area of path = Area of larger circular park – Area of smaller circular park

⇒ 1386 – π(r – 7)²

⇒ 1386 – π(21 – 7)²

⇒ 1386 – π(14)²

⇒ 1386 – π(196)

⇒ 1386 – (22/7 × 196)

⇒ (1386 – 616) m²

⇒ 770 m²

**∴ The required area of the path is 770 m²**

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a launch vehicle technology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** MSLV.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Launch vehicles or launch systems** are used to **transport spacecraft** from the **Earth's surface into space.**
 
• To establish a sustainable orbit, a **velocity **of roughly** Mach 25 or about 8 km/s** is required.
 
• In **1964** during a test flight, **NASA's largest launch vehicle**, the **Saturn SA-5**, sent a record-breaking **19 tonnes** into orbit. The **first American Gemini flight**, an unpiloted test that made four orbits and was successfully recovered, took place on April 8, 1964.
 
• The development of launch vehicles in** India** began in the early** 1970s.**
 
• In **1980,** the first experimental **Satellite Launch Vehicle (SLV-3)** was built.
 
• In **1992**, an augmented version of this,** ASLV**, was successfully introduced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Satellite Launch Vehicle-3 (SLV-3):**

 
 
• It was **India’s first **experimental satellite launch vehicle, which was an all solid, **four-stage vehicle **weighing 17 tonnes.
 
• It had a** height of 22m **and it was capable of placing **40 kg class** payloads in** Low Earth Orbit (LEO).**
 
• The flight of SLV3, launch on **July 18, 1980,** from** Sriharikota Range (SHAR),** successfully placed** Rohini satellite, RS-1**, into orbit, thereby making** India** the** sixth member** of an exclusive club of **space-faring.**
 
 
 
• **Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle (ASLV)**:
 
 
• The Augmented Satellite Launch Spacecraft (ASLV) was created as a** low-cost intermediate vehicle** for demonstrating and validating key technologies. 
 
• The **23.8 m tall** ASLV was constructed as a **five-stage, all-solid propellant vehicle** with a mission of orbiting **150 kg class **satellites into 400 km circular orbits, with a lift-off weight of 40 tonnes.
 
• **Four developmental flights **were carried out as part of the ASLV programme:
 

 
 
• On **March 24, 1987**, the first developmental flight took place.

questions.question: Which of the following methods can be used for separating a mixture of NaCl and NH₄CI?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sublimation** is the process of converting stuff from a** solid to a gaseous state** without passing through a** liquid state**.
 
• Sublimation is the term used to describe the process of** snow and ice **converting into **water vapour **in the air without first melting into water.
 
• Sublimation can be used to separate an** ammonium chloride and common salt mixture.**
 
• In a china dish, the mixture is set on a tripod stand.
 
• An **inverted glass funnel **is used to cover the china dish.
 
• To keep the ammonium chloride vapours from escaping into the atmosphere, a **loose cotton plug** is placed in the funnel's upper, open end.
 
• A burner is used to heat the china dish. Ammonium chloride transforms into** white vapours **when heated.
 
• When these vapours come into touch with the funnel's chilly inner walls, they rise up and transform to **solid ammonium chloride.**
 
• As a result, **pure ammonium chloride sublimates** on the inner walls of the funnel and can be removed.
 
• Common salt remains behind in the china dish.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• Crystallization is the process by which a **solid forms**, where the **atoms or molecules** are highly **organized into a structure** known as a crystal. 
 
• **Precipitation** from a solution, **freezing, **and, more rarely,** direct deposition from a gas** are some of the ways crystals form.
 
• Crystallization is a technique that has long been used in the **purification of substances.**

 It is used daily in making- **Steel, eggnog and hard tack candy.**
 
 
 
• **Centrifugation__:**
 __
 
• Centrifugation is a **mechanical process **that separates particles from a solution based on their **size, shape, density, medium viscosity, and rotor speed **using centrifugal force.
 
• Putting **milk **into a machine to **separate the cream** from the milk is an example of centrifugation.

 Centrifugation is a technique for treating **wastewater and sewage.**
 
• It is used to** remove metal shavings** and other particles from **industrial lubricants.**
 
 
 
• **Chromatography__:**
 
 
• Chromatography is a technique for **separating the components**, or solutes, of a mixture based on the relative amounts of each solute distributed between a flowing fluid stream, known as the **mobile phase**, and a **stationary phase** that is contiguous.
 
• The mixture's various components move through the stationary phase at different speeds, leading them to separate from one another.
 
• Which substances go more swiftly or slowly, and how they are divided, is determined by the characteristics of the** individual mobile and stationary phases.**
 
• These different travel times are termed **retention time.**
